record.context_brief: Colored perfect matchings in bipartite graphs
record.original_question: What is the computational complexity of deciding, for a 2-edge-coloured bipartite graph B=(U,V,E), whether B contains two edge-disjoint perfect matchings M1 and M2 such that every edge of M1 has colour 1 while M2 may use edges of either colour?

evidence.quote: Question 2.14. What is the complexity of the following problem: given a 2-edge-coloured bipartite graph B = (U, V, E); decide whether B has two edge-disjoint perfect matchings M1, M2 so that every edge of M1 has colour 1, while M2 may use edges of both colours?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B = (U, V, E)$ be a bipartite graph with $|U| = |V|$, equipped with an edge 2-coloring $c: E \to \{1, 2\}$. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem:

INPUT: A 2-edge-colored bipartite graph $B = (U, V, E)$ as above.

QUESTION: Do there exist two edge-disjoint perfect matchings $M_1, M_2 \subseteq E$ of $B$ such that every edge of $M_1$ has color $1$ (while $M_2$ may contain edges of either color $1$ or color $2$)?

In particular, decide whether this problem is in P, NP-complete, or has some other precise complexity classification.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive resolution of this specific complexity question. Related problems on edge-colored bipartite matching (e.g., exact matching, labeled matching) are studied, with exact matching famously known to admit a randomized parallel algorithm but no known deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, while labeled variants can be NP-hard. No source found explicitly classifies the complexity of this two-matching variant, so the status is treated as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Exact Matching: Algorithms and Related Problems
status_evidence.snippet: The exact perfect matching problem... no deterministic polynomial-time algorithm is known, even for bipartite graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related colored matching problems in bipartite graphs remain of unresolved complexity.

status_evidence.title: On Complexity and Approximability of the Labeled Maximum/Perfect Matching Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Labeled maximum matching problem in edge-colored graphs has known hardness results.
status_evidence.claim: Edge-colored matching problems exhibit a range of complexity behaviors, with several variants NP-hard.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of a disjoint matching problem on bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Disjoint matching problems with constraints on bipartite graphs can be NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: The general framework of edge-disjoint constrained matchings on bipartite graphs is known to contain NP-hard cases.
